acceptance: The throughput stream gate's timeout recording is covered by a test that fails if it regresses.
context: Gap noted by the review-fix implementer in the run-timeout effort.
description:
## Problem
In #4435 the throughput runner's per-stream gate (benchbox/core/throughput/runner.py) was switched from the read-only `run_deadline_expired()` to `run_stop_requested()`, which records the timeout. Every other gate of that class got a dedicated test; this one did not, so a regression back to a read-only check (streams skipped with `deadline.timeout` left None, so `adapter.run_benchmark(timeout_seconds=...)` returns an unmarked short result) would not be caught.

## Change
Add a test: a stream whose next query starts after the deadline passed stops, the deadline's timeout is recorded, and the result is marked timed out through the adapter path.

## Decision gates
Test only; if the test exposes a product defect, fix it in the same pull request and say so. Patch only seams the module owns (`wait_for_completed` etc.), never stdlib.

## Verification rubric
The test fails when the gate is changed back to `run_deadline_expired()` (show it) and passes on develop; `make pr-preflight` exits 0.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
